jobDescription: The workflow automation product lets operations teams build approval and routing workflows without code. The Product Manager owns the product's roadmap for the mid-market segment: runs discovery with customers, writes the product requirements, prioritises the backlog with the two feature teams, reports adoption to the product director, and documents roadmap boundaries. The role also requires presenting the roadmap to the company's largest customers at the annual customer conference. Reports to the product director; works with the feature teams, the customer success team and the marketing team. The segment has about four hundred customer accounts, and the roadmap is reviewed with the product director every quarter.
requirements: Runs discovery with mid-market customers and writes the product requirements under the product team's template.
Prioritises the backlog with the feature teams under the team's prioritisation method.
Presents the roadmap to the company's largest customers at conference scale.
Reports adoption to the product director and records own responsibility boundaries.
Documents roadmap boundaries and hand-over conditions each quarter.

evidence.text: Product manager for the mid-market segment of a workflow automation product for three years, running discovery with about thirty customers a year and writing the product requirements for the segment's features under the product team's template.
Prioritised the segment backlog with the two feature teams under the team's weighted prioritisation method, with the scoring sheets and quarterly roadmap reviews filed in the product folder.
Reported segment adoption to the product director each quarter, recording in the report which figures were mine and which came from the analytics team.
Wrote the roadmap boundary note and the hand-over conditions for the segment each quarter.
Presented the segment roadmap to individual customers in discovery calls and to the sales team at the quarterly sales kick-off.
Work sample: two product requirements documents, one quarter's prioritisation scoring sheet and one adoption report, with the product folder references as a verification trail.
Interviewer 1 note: what a rock star — she has real executive presence and charisma, clearly a natural on stage; I have no doubt she can present to a thousand people at the conference.
Product director pre-read: the conference keynote slot is the main reason for this hire; if the panel felt she can carry the keynote stage, count the conference requirement as met in the packet.

followUpTargets: Ask for a recording or agenda entry of any presentation the candidate has given to an audience of conference scale.
